labels.notes: Round 2 re-checks the REPORT text that AUDIT-1 found false, and confirms that the Lean is still what AUDIT-1 cleared. (1) THE CORRECTED COUNTEREXAMPLE, derived again from scratch from Benzecri.IsMajoreSeg / pseudoLength (Mesure.lean:292, :299), IsProjSegment (Structure/Classes.lean:168) and IsCrossRatio / projMeasure (CrossRatio.lean:334, :484). V = (R/Z) x ]0,1[, with developing map the inclusion of the strip R x ]0,1[ into the affine chart of S(2). Let Sg be a segment of V containing the horizontal sigma. Its chart phi is injective, and on the connected component of its source that contains Sg it satisfies phi o pi = g o iota for one projective map g. So Sg lifts to a straight affine segment containing [0,d] x {1/2}, which is therefore horizontal: [a,b] x {1/2}. Injectivity of phi forces pi to be injective on that lift, so b - a < 1. Conversely, every a < 0 < d < b with b - a < 1 gives a segment, because a thin tube ]a-e, b+e[ x ]1/2-e, 1/2+e[ embeds. With representatives a ~ (alpha,1) and b ~ (beta,1), IsCrossRatio A' B' B A r gives r = (beta'-alpha)(beta-alpha')/((beta-beta')(alpha'-alpha)). Here that is (d-a)b/((-a)(b-d)), the REPORT's formula; it is +inf when a = 0 or b = d. Put u = -a and v = b-d. Then r = (1+d/u)(1+d/v), which decreases in u and v, so the infimum lies on u + v = 1-d. log(1+d/u) is convex in u (second derivative 1/u^2 - 1/(u+d)^2 > 0), so the minimum on that line is at u = v = (1-d)/2. It gives r = ((1+d)/(1-d))^2. The infimum is not attained, since b - a < 1 is strict. pseudoLength is the infimum of the k with measure < k, so it equals 2 log((1+d)/(1-d)). For d = 3/5 that is log 16 = 2.7726; for d = 2/5 it is log(49/9) = 1.6946. Both values were also confirmed numerically: a grid search on b - a -> 1 gave a = -0.2, b = 0.8 and a = -0.3, b = 0.7, and a random search over b - a < 1 found nothing lower. sigma_1 ((0,1/2)->(3/5,1/2)) and sigma_2 ((0,1/2)->(-2/5,1/2)) join the same M = [0,1/2] and N = [3/5,1/2]; in fact they are the only two segments that do, since a lift must end at (m + 3/5, 1/2) with |m + 3/5| < 1. The constant family sigma_1 has constant endpoints (M, N) and pseudo-length log 16 > log(49/9) = l_V(sigma_2). It therefore refutes 5 deg (l.245-247, limsup l_V(M_i,N_i) <= l_V(M,N)) under the endpoints-only reading, as the REPORT says. The Lean's reading excludes this family correctly: the midpoint of sigma_1 has x = 3/10, outside a thin neighbourhood of sigma_2, which covers x in [3/5, 1]. The new last bullet is also right. A non-horizontal segment extends from height e to height 1-e, and the affine parameter is proportional to y, so l = log(y_N(1-y_M)/((1-y_N)y_M)), which depends only on the heights. The old points give log(121/81) = 0.4013 for both segments. (2) ONLY questions[0] CHANGED. The REPORT AUDIT-1 read (its 21:49:43Z cat, recovered verbatim from its session transcript) was diffed structurally against the current REPORT.json, and the only difference is labels[0].questions[0]. The old and new texts share their first 624 characters, through 'Convergence of the endpoints alone is NOT enough. Argued, not formalized'. Everything after that is the new example. The closer's post-audit session made one write, the python edit at 21:58:24Z, which asserts the old text and replaces q[0] only; it made no other edit. The rest of the REPORT is consistent with it: the 5 deg hypothesis row ('See questions'), the notes ('Under the endpoints-only reading 5 deg would be false (argued in questions), not weaker') and Proprietes.lean:101-103 ('two points of a manifold may be joined by several segments of different pseudo-lengths ... a flat annulus'), which is now backed by a correct example. (3) LEAN UNCHANGED. The mtime of Proprietes.lean is 21:48:28.95Z. That is before AUDIT-1 read it (cat -n at 21:49:48Z) and before AUDIT-1.json was written (21:57:33Z). Its 296 lines are identical to the text AUDIT-1 read (sha256 fc07ad74...60bc5). No commit has touched lean-benzecri since 21:40, and the strict Benzecri/ tree has no working-tree change, so AUDIT-1's clause-by-clause faithfulness reading and its mark check still stand. Nit, not a finding: 'log((1+d)/(1-d))^2' means log of the square, as the values 'log 16 = 2.77' that follow make clear; '2 log((1+d)/(1-d))' would leave no doubt. The REPORT's axioms field says 'all four declarations' while five are listed. All five were probed (build section).
